$schema: Session DevNotes - deviations, discoveries, decisions captured during build

notes.content: Wired EventsSection into LayerForm as part of the LayerForm rewrite (TG3.1.2) rather than as a separate follow-up step (TG3.2.3). Same end state — EventsSection mounted at the bottom of every canonical SceneObject form with onChange committing the full array via 'events' key (deepMerge replaces arrays wholesale).

Toggling Fill ON commits the full transform patch with explicit-mode fields set to undefined ({mode:'fill', x:undefined, y:undefined, width:undefined, height:undefined, anchor:undefined}). deepMerge sets these properties to undefined on the existing transform; JSON.stringify drops them at save time. Toggling Fill OFF restores defaults (x=0, y=0, width='auto', height='auto', anchor='top-left') while preserving the prior rotation/scale.

InspectorPanel dispatch uses data-shape rather than path heuristics: layer.layer → SubLayerForm; (!layer.transform && layer.type==='media') → MediaChildForm; else → LayerForm. This correctly routes canonical SceneObjects with nested children (added by CP2 recursive rendering) to LayerForm, not to the legacy MediaChildForm.
ClipSelect import remained on MediaChildForm (legacy foreign-media child still uses properties.clip until CP5). LayerForm dropped it entirely — canonical Appearance has no clip field.

Reused the same Tailwind classes already used by RangedInput's number input and BlendSelect (bg-[#222], rounded-sm, focus:border-[#4a8fc2]) for the string input and enum select inside ManifestPropertyField, instead of the ad-hoc classes shown in the plan. Keeps the inspector visually consistent.

Manifest narrowing on containerEntry uses `'manifest' in containerEntry` rather than a type guard helper. AssetContainer has no manifest field, so `'manifest' in entry` cleanly narrows to ModuleEntry without an extra import.

Grab-bag fallback in LayerForm renders ONLY when no manifest is attached — when a manifest exists, it is authoritative even if it has zero properties (the section then renders nothing). Per plan: legacy data without manifest still surfaces, but a module with a manifest controls the inspector exactly.

SlotsSection commits the FULL slots array on every appearance edit instead of using patchFromDottedKey('slots.${i}.appearance.${key}', value) as the plan suggested. Reason: deepMerge() in editor-store treats arrays as opaque (line 77: `Array.isArray(target) → return patch`), so patching with `{ slots: { 0: {...} } }` would replace the slots array with a plain object. Following the same pattern EventsSection uses for its full-array commits.

AssetSwapDropdown takes (assetId, assetType, currentFile), not just a single containerId as the plan implied. SlotsSection resolves slot.asset against the registry to derive assetType + currentFile (mirroring LayerForm's pattern). Falls back to a ReadonlyValue if the registry doesn't yet have the entry.

Slot keeps its own `appearance` (Appearance from CP1). Renderer applies opacity/blend on the foreignObject and hue/fit on the inner leaf element. clip-path is mirrored from the SVG anchor element onto the foreignObject so video clips to letter shapes via the SVG-authored fill-clip — no per-slot clip field needed.

Scene migration dropped 47 child entries from codecaine-logo (46 baked sub-layer overrides + 1 in-text-fire foreign child) → 1 slot entry. Hierarchy panel becomes dramatically lighter: codecaine-logo now exposes a single `in-text-fire` slot instead of 40+ nested rows.

Export route rewrites absolute paths in copied artifacts so the bundle works under file:// or any static host. Both registry.json files have entry.file/entry.path values rewritten from '/foo/...' to './foo/...'. Renderer source files are run through a regex that replaces (["'(])/(assets|modules|fonts)/ with $1./$2/ — this catches the hard-coded fetch('/assets/registry.json') / fetch('/modules/registry.json') in asset-registry.js and any stray absolute paths in the asset-renderers. Plan task 6.3.2.3 implied loadRegistry already supported relative defaults; it doesn't, so the export route patches it instead of changing the runtime renderer (which still needs absolute paths under Next.js).

Audio assets ship as a directory copy (start-cue/start-cue.js + sibling files) rather than a single file copy, because the registry.json `file` for audio points at a JS wrapper that may load sibling .mp3/.wav. Image/video/glyph entries copy a single file. Modules (effects + components) always copy the full containing directory so manifest.json and CSS siblings ride along.

loadProject() / discoverScenes() preserves the legacy directory-scan fallback (used when no project.json exists), so dev scenes that haven't been registered in project.json still appear on the dashboard with isEntry=false. Today the only project (codecaine) is fully registered, so the fallback is dormant.

Verified the exported zip with a static HTTP server — index.html, project.json, scene.json, registries, the patched asset-registry.js, press-start manifest, and font file all return 200. file:// testing requires manual browser open (no headless tooling in build context); the static-server smoke test gives equivalent confidence in the asset graph.
